newsitem.title: USA: FBI returns engagement ring from TWA wreckage.
newsitem.headline: FBI returns engagement ring from TWA wreckage.

text.p: After months of waiting, a Connecticut woman Monday received the diamond engagement ring her fiance was carrying when he was killed in the crash of TWA Flight 800 in July.

In a private meeting at FBI offices in New York, lead investigator James Kallstrom gave Julie Stuart the 1.6-karat diamond ring salvagers found floating in the Atlantic Ocean in its maroon box July 18, one day after plane went down with all its passengers and crew.

"I think it was pretty miraculous that it was found at all -- it's so small in a huge ocean -- so I think it was meant for me to have it," Stuart told reporters after receiving the ring from Kallstrom, head of the FBI in New York.
The 31-year-old personnel manager was going to marry Andrew Krukar, one of the 230 victims of the crash.
Krukar, who met Stuart at the company where they both worked, had planned a rendezvous in Paris July 19 to make their engagement official by presenting her with the ring.

TWA Flight 800 crashed off Long Island without warning just minutes after taking off from Kennedy airport for Paris. The cause of the disaster has not yet been declared, but authorities suspect mechanical failure, a bomb or a missile doomed the Boeing 747.

Stuart, who lives in Bridgewater, Connecticut, knew the ring had been recovered from the debris because it appeared in a Paris Match magazine photograph in August. She and Krukar's family submitted pages of documentation to authorities to prove its ownership.

It had been kept as evidence, like all other personal belongings from the aircraft's wreckage. Authorities said they were considering publishing a catalogue of all the "unassociated items" found to help victims' relatives identify them.
